children: Shares of Ascendis Pharma rose Monday after entering into a settlement agreement with BioMarin Pharmaceutical, resolving all pending patent disputes concerning its rare disease drug, Yuviwel.

Under the terms of the agreement, Ascendis agreed to pay BioMarin a 20% royalty on net sales of Yuviwel in the U.S., retroactively to its first commercial sale, and an 18% royalty on net sales in the EU, Brazil and South Korea through May 2030.
In return, BioMarin will grant Ascendis a worldwide patent license for Yuviwel for current treatment of achondroplasia and hypochondroplasia, as well as any potential future indications.
Achondroplasia is a common type of short-limbed dwarfism, while the related hypochondroplasia is a milder form of genetic skeletal disorder.

Both companies agreed to dismiss all pending patent-infringement litigation before the U.S. International Trade Commission as well as and regulatory proceedings in the U.S., Germany, Denmark, South Korea and Brazil.
